clue.text: Composure as two thirds majority of Labour MP changed

indicators.note: changed tells us the selected letters and MP are rearranged into a new order
two thirds of a six-letter word is its first four letters, the larger share of Labour

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A politician keeps calm while a two-thirds Labour majority shifts in Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two thirds majority of' takes LABO from Labour; 'changed' rearranges LABO plus MP.
explanation.definitionFit: Aplomb is self-assurance and poise, a near synonym of calm composure.

clue.text: Garment to fasten round one before dark (French)

indicators.note: round says the fastening word goes around the numeral

parts.note: to peg is to fasten, as washing on a line
I is the Roman numeral one
noir is French for black or dark

explanation.surface: A garment is pinned around someone before a night out in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: A peignoir is a woman's light dressing gown or negligee.

clue.text: Run faster? Not in football gear

parts.note: not in means out
strip is a team's kit of shirt, shorts and socks

explanation.surface: A footballer wonders if speed comes from playing without kit.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a football team's kit is called its strip.
explanation.definitionFit: To outpace a rival is to go faster and leave them behind.

clue.text: Generous so-called lady of the theatre

definitions.meaning: Lady ..., the charitable character in Farquhar's play The Beaux' Stratagem

explanation.definitionFit: Openhanded means giving freely, and the charitable Lady of Farquhar's stage comedy bears the name.

clue.text: Reader, for example, has a short book about rebel leader

indicators.note: about means going round, so the first pair of pieces is wrapped round the rebel

parts.note: Mic. is the short form of Micah, a book of the Bible
Jack Cade led the Kentish rebellion of 1450

explanation.surface: A university reader has written a brief biography of a revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: A Reader is a senior university teaching rank in Britain, just below professor, so 'Reader' is a title, not someone reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A Reader is one example of a university lecturer, i.e. a scholar holding a teaching post.

clue.text: Book a room in Miss Allen's home town

annotationWithheld.why: Book a room in Miss Allen's home town (1,5,2,7): A + STUDY + IN fit, but no source found for SCARLET as Miss Allen's home town, so that piece cannot be explained honestly.
annotationWithheld.clue: Book a room in Miss Allen's home town

clue.text: These animals are in sleeping quarters before freeze comes

indicators.note: before places the bedroom word ahead of the frozen water word

parts.note: a dorm, short for dormitory, is a shared bedroom
ice is frozen water

explanation.surface: Creatures stay in bed before the winter frost sets in.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface fits: these rodents hibernate through winter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormice are small rodents famous for hibernating, so they are creatures.

clue.text: Wrong mark is accepted

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for the mark, old German currency
taken as written
taken means accepted

explanation.surface: The wrong mark has been allowed to stand.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistaken means in error, incorrect.

clue.text: Get about a pound to work for musicians

parts.note: C is circa, about
oncer is old slang for a one-pound note
taken as written

explanation.surface: Earn around a quid for working with a band.
explanation.walkthrough: ONCER is old British slang for a one-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: A concerto is a musical composition for a soloist and orchestra.

clue.text: Young girl bound, we hear, to be suspicious

indicators.note: we hear signals that the words are to be judged by their sound when spoken

parts.note: a young girl is a miss, and bound means trussed: miss trussed

explanation.surface: A tied-up young girl understandably grows wary.
explanation.definitionFit: To mistrust is to doubt or be wary of something, being suspicious of it.

clue.text: A pair with a single child can

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, a single
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A couple with an only child makes a little family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' is slang for jail, not a tin or a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Can is slang for jail, a place where convicts are locked up.

clue.text: One Name reported to be established in an office

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
reported means stated, said

explanation.surface: One person's name is said to be on the register of a company office.
explanation.definitionFit: To be put formally into a post is to be installed, inducted into a job.

clue.text: End with a pound in sterling

indicators.note: in places the article and the pound inside the word for sterling

parts.note: sterling silver is fine, of high purity
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Finishing with a single pound in British currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sterling' is the adjective meaning excellent or pure, i.e. fine, not money.
explanation.definitionFit: A finale is the closing part of a show or piece of music, its conclusion.

clue.text: Break in finger — put right elsewhere

indicators.note: put with elsewhere says one letter of the words in finger is shifted to a different spot

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fractured finger has to be set straight somewhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put ... elsewhere' moves the R (right) of IN FINGER to a new position.
explanation.definitionFit: To infringe a rule is to violate or breach it.

clue.text: Stick with prize fighter's protective equipment

parts.note: to gum is to stick
a shield is a trophy awarded as a prize

explanation.surface: A trophy is glued onto a boxer's kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prize fighter' wants to be read together, but 'prize' gives SHIELD and the definition starts at 'fighter's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer wears a mouthguard to protect the teeth.

clue.text: Produce a hairstyle

explanation.definitionFit: A harvest is farm produce, and a short haircut is also called by the same name.

clue.text: Quickly repeated blow

indicators.note: repeated says the word for blow appears twice in a row

parts.note: a chop is a cutting blow

explanation.surface: A rapid volley of karate strikes.
explanation.definitionFit: This is pidgin-derived slang urging haste, meaning hurry up.

clue.text: Inspection previously completed

parts.note: once means formerly, previously
over means finished, completed

explanation.surface: A check was carried out earlier and is now done.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick look over something is a brief examination.

clue.text: Very interested in certain topics

indicators.note: in signals the letters lie inside the run of the words certain topics

explanation.surface: Someone who is keen on particular subjects.
explanation.definitionFit: Being into something is idiomatic for being enthusiastic about it.

clue.text: Offensive order restricting church

indicators.note: restricting suggests the order holds the church within it

parts.note: an indent is an official order for goods
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A rule is imposed that limits what the church may do.
explanation.walkthrough: An INDENT is a requisition order, especially in the army.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecent means improper or shocking, offending public taste.

clue.text: Get a lute constructed for lessons

indicators.note: constructed implies building the letters of get a lute into something new

explanation.surface: Buy a lute that has been made for your music classes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutelage is instruction or tuition given by a teacher.

clue.text: Rugby bully in second half upset an opponent

indicators.note: in puts the letter for second inside the rest of the wordplay
upset says the letters of half are knocked into a new order

parts.note: in team games each player marks his man, the opponent he is assigned

explanation.surface: A rugby player throws his weight around after the interval and floors an opposing player.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby is the school, not the game: Flashman is the bully in Tom Brown's School Days. 'upset' turns HALF into FLAH; 'in' puts S inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Flashman is the tormentor of younger boys at Rugby School in Thomas Hughes's novel.

clue.text: Reckoned it's the fourth illustration

parts.note: a figure is a numbered picture in a book
D is the fourth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Judging it to be the fourth diagram in the book.
explanation.walkthrough: Figures in books are labelled A, B, C, D, so the fourth is FIGURE D.
explanation.definitionFit: Figured is informal for calculated or concluded.

clue.text: Hock for a toast

definitions.meaning: to pawn something, leave it as security

explanation.definitionFit: To pawn is to give as security for a loan, and an old word for drinking someone's health is the same.

clue.text: Competitors allowed to enter various heats

indicators.note: to enter puts the word for allowed inside the shuffled letters
various suggests the letters of heats are mixed into a different order

parts.note: let means allowed

explanation.surface: Contestants are permitted into several qualifying races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heats' looks like part of the sporting surface, but it is the anagram fodder, giving ATHES.
explanation.definitionFit: Athletes are sports contestants, those taking part in races and field events.

clue.text: Last of English claims is rubbish, according to Scots

indicators.note: Last of takes only the final letter of the word English

parts.note: avers means claims, asserts

explanation.surface: The final bit of English assertion is nonsense, the Scots say.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland, talk of this kind is nonsense, foolish chatter.

clue.text: Lord's supporter wants one in cricket side to call back

indicators.note: in puts the numeral one inside the cricket term

parts.note: leg is the on side of a cricket field
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: back says the word for call is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: to name is to call

explanation.surface: A peer's backer wants someone on the leg side of a cricket field to phone again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns NAME into EMAN. Leg side is the half of a cricket field behind the batsman's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A feudal vassal owed loyal service to his lord, being his sworn follower.

clue.text: One prepared to take off or do a strip, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters of do a strip could be arranged in another way

explanation.surface: Someone ready to remove their clothes, or else to perform a striptease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take off' means mimic, not undress, though the strip-tease surface wants it otherwise.
explanation.definitionFit: A parodist mimics or satirises others, and to take off someone is to imitate them.

clue.text: Most parts of Fiji are scattered like this

definitions.text: Most parts of Fiji are scattered like this

parts.words: Most parts of Fiji are scattered like this
parts.note: three of the four letters of the written word Fiji, the I, J and I, carry a dot, and the islands are spread about the ocean

explanation.definitionFit: Spread here and there like spots, as islands across a sea are.
